Does the IP address of my cell phone change when I power-cycle it?

There's a decent chance it will if you're not on WiFi. I'm actually curious about this, I'm gunna test it out brb.

Edit: Yeah, my IP changed with a power cycle. http://imgur.com/a/7Cx6L

Generally, when a device is assigned an IP address, the DHCP server links that IP address to the devices MAC address for a set amount of time, usually for 24 hours. So unless you can change your device's MAC address (spoofing) or reset the DHCP server to clear its cache, you're going to keep getting the same IP address assigned. The only sure fire way is to leave to device off/disconnected until the server clears your MAC address from it IP table.

Mobile IP addresses work completely different than fixed line internet. I've seen devices go through 10 different IP addresses within an hour. It largely depends on location and quality of signal and type of network.
If you are on 3G/4G it can change at any point in time. It is less likely to happen if you are not moving and have a strong signal, but there is still no guarantee.

It should change simply by cycling through airplane mode. People in cars and other scenarios make it almost impossible for a cell-tower to reserve an IP address for your specific device. Hell, even just tower-jumping will probably change your IP every now and then.

I do it all the time when I need to grab a disposable IP for... reasons.

Sure but cellular routing is different than normal tcp/ip routing. Your provider tracks you by your phones IMSI number.

Imagine the hashtag system that exists on twitter and Facebook ect. Except you can only use existing hashtags on your posts. These hashtags can be created by users in the same way you can create a subVOAT or Subreddit.

People can then use hashtags that they are subscribed to. But the interesting part of the idea is that Other people can apply hashtags to your thread. This means the op has placed filtering on the post itself and then you have inflected filtering by all users who decide that they want to add more filtering options. to add your post to hashtags you may not be subscribed to.

Lets say for example you make a post about a cool accomplishment and you are subscribed to the hashtag, #HappyStory This means that you have a #HappyStory +1 on the post when it goes on to your wall. Here, perhaps, is a practical criterion for resolving the demarcation problem: the conduct of scientists as reflected in the pragmatic usefulness of an idea. That is, does the revolutionary new idea generate any interest on the part of working scientists for adoption in their research programs, produce any new lines of research, lead to any new discoveries, or influence any existing hypotheses, models, paradigms or world­views? We can demarcate science from pseudoscience less by what science is and more by what scientists do. Science is a set of methods aimed at testing hypotheses and building theories. If a community of scientists actively adopts a new idea and if that idea then spreads through the field and is incorporated into research that produces useful knowledge reflected in presentations, publications, and especially new lines of inquiry and research, chances are it is science.

This demarcation criterion of usefulness has the advantage of being bottom-up instead of top-down, egalitarian instead of elitist, nondiscriminatory instead of prejudicial.
